# Component and scope glob cases, shared by the Go matcher (internal/pathglob)
# and the Rust one (engine build_globset). Both sides read this file, so a
# divergence fails a test instead of being discovered on a user's repository.
#
# pathglob's doc comment has always claimed its semantics match "what globset
# does on the Rust side". Nothing checked it. That is the same shape as the
# defect where five Go matchers disagreed about `in: ["**"]` — one pattern
# string, several implementations, agreement asserted only in prose.
#
# Format: <pattern> <TAB> <path> <TAB> match|no-match
# Lines starting with # and blank lines are ignored.

# The catch-all. globset matches "**" against any path; the Go side needed a
# segment-wise walk to do the same, and one copy used path.Match, which treats
# "*" as not crossing "/" and so matched nothing.
**	main.go	match
**	internal/domain/user.go	match
**	a/b/c/d/e.go	match
**	internal	match

# dir/** covers the directory itself as well as everything under it. globset
# alone does not — "src/domain/**" requires at least one further segment — which
# is why build_globset also adds the bare pattern.
internal/**	internal	match
internal/**	internal/domain	match
internal/**	internal/domain/user.go	match
internal/**	cmd/main.go	no-match
internal/**	other/internal/domain	no-match

# A trailing slash names a directory.
internal/	internal	match
internal/	internal/domain	match
internal/	cmd	no-match

# A bare name with no metacharacters covers the tree below it, and must not
# match a sibling that merely shares a prefix. `strings.Contains` was the
# original implementation here: "domain" also claimed "subdomain".
internal	internal	match
internal	internal/domain	match
internal	internalx	no-match
internal	x/internal	no-match

# Anchoring: a pattern matches from the start of the path. A pattern that
# matched anywhere would silence findings the author never named.
gen/**	gen/a.go	match
gen/**	internal/gen/a.go	no-match
**/gen/**	internal/gen/a.go	match
**/gen/**	gen/a.go	match

# Single-segment wildcards do not cross a separator.
internal/*/store	internal/user/store	match
internal/*/store	internal/store	no-match
internal/*/store	internal/a/b/store	no-match
*.go	main.go	match
*.go	internal/main.go	no-match
**/*.go	internal/main.go	match
**/*.go	main.go	match

# Deeper mixes of ** and named segments.
**/adapter/**	internal/adapter	match
**/adapter/**	internal/adapter/postgres/db.go	match
**/adapter/**	internal/adapters/postgres	no-match
cmd/**/main.go	cmd/api/main.go	match
cmd/**/main.go	cmd/main.go	match
cmd/**/main.go	internal/cmd/api/main.go	no-match

# Single-character wildcard.
v?/**	v1/handler.go	match
v?/**	v10/handler.go	no-match
